key_insight: UNSM can substantially alter the local hardness of Cr3C2–NiCr coatings, but the response depends strongly on the deposition route and treatment settings.
engineering_relevance: For wear-resistant thermal-spray coatings, both process route and post-treatment parameters must be tuned together because they can shift surface hardness and scratch-related morphology in different ways.
method: Detonation-sprayed and HVOF Cr3C2–NiCr coatings were post-treated by ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification (UNSM).
Two static loads (20, 30 N) and two vibration amplitudes (20, 30 µm) were applied to four samples per deposition route.
Hardness was measured instrumentally at 300 mN load with a 10 s dwell, and post-scratch SEM was used to inspect surface morphology.
evidence_signal: Measured hardness ranged from 820–970 HV for detonation-sprayed coatings and 546–1165 HV for HVOF coatings, with SEM showing heterogeneous contrast and crack-like features after scratching.
watch_item: The scratch SEM observations are qualitative and do not clearly separate damage caused by UNSM from pre-existing coating condition, so scratch resistance ranking remains uncertain.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
